claim: A selectorless Service plus a manually-created EndpointSlice can silently fail to route any traffic if the Service's port is unnamed while the EndpointSlice's port of the same number is named (or vice versa); kube-proxy's internal Service-to-endpoint mapping requires port-name consistency and otherwise installs a REJECT rule.
stance_target: selectorless Service + manual EndpointSlice is a drop-in, low-risk way to expose non-pod backends
scope_conditions: kube-proxy iptables mode, reproduced on K3s v1.28.7+k3s1 (Kubernetes core bug, not K3s-specific per maintainer)
quoted_support: I see you are defining ports with a name in the endpointslice but without a name in the service which is breaking our internal mapping of service to endpoints. Making both the ports either named or un-named should solve the issue.

claim: When the port-name mismatch occurs, kube-proxy installs an iptables REJECT rule with the comment 'has no endpoints' and returns icmp-port-unreachable, even though kubectl get endpointslice shows the correct backend IP present and healthy.
stance_target: manual EndpointSlice misconfiguration is easy to detect from standard tooling
quoted_support: -A KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.43.202.125/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "debug-endpoints/mariadb has no endpoints" -m tcp --dport 3306 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable

claim: kubectl describe service continues to display 'Endpoints: <none>' even after a manual EndpointSlice backend is correctly routing traffic, because kubectl reads the legacy Endpoints object, which is never auto-populated from manually-created EndpointSlices (mirroring only runs Endpoints-to-EndpointSlice, not the reverse).
stance_target: standard kubectl output reliably reflects the health of a manual-EndpointSlice backend
scope_conditions: kubectl as of 2024, confirmed unresolved as of issue closure (only a doc/UX gap, not a routing bug)
quoted_support: If you manually create EndpointSlices, the associated Endpoints for the same Service doesn't get autopopulated (and that's where kubectl is looking).
